$comment: What each job must leave behind and how the owner verifies it before the next step. Output hashes are unknown until a job runs; every check is local and offline after `aws s3 cp`. Every job writes model/stack-check.json; a job on a stack that differs from requirements-train.txt fails unless FLH_ALLOW_STACK_MISMATCH=1, which no rendered job sets.
naming: Job names are flh-extractor-<role>-<UTC yyyymmdd-hhmmss>, one role per rendered file; outputs land under s3://<BUCKET>/extractor/output/<job name>/ (readiness-checks.json proves names and prefixes are distinct).

checks: run_manifest.json: train_sha256 and dev_sha256 equal input-manifest.json; steps == 12; smoke true; suitable_for_production false; model_profile qwen3.5-4b; chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking: false}; skipped_too_long == 0
run_manifest.json files: every listed sha256 matches the extracted file
losses.jsonl: 12 finite train_loss values; dev_loss at steps 6 and 12
timing: seconds / 12 = seconds per step; projected experiment = 234 steps x seconds per step + 10 dev evaluations; must be <= 9000 s (the 10800 s bound with margin)
272 rows: the 200 frozen evaluation prompts, then the 72 challenge_test prompts, in prompt order (shard a)
every row has output_text, generated_tokens and stopped; count stopped == max_new_tokens (truncation)
BillableTimeInSeconds and rows give the inference rate; shard b (200 rows) fits the same bound
200 rows: the rb probe prompts in prompt order (shard b)
concatenate a then b as qwen3.5-4b-untuned predictions; `compare` accounts for every slice row (a missing shard shows as 200 or 272 missing_prediction rows, never as a smaller slice)
run_manifest.json: hashes equal input-manifest.json; smoke false; suitable_for_production false; skipped_too_long == 0; steps == 234
losses.jsonl: dev loss does not rise at two consecutive evaluations (promotion-check and decision-report read it)
the adapter is extracted and copied to s3://<BUCKET>/extractor/adapters/<job>/ for predict-eval-a and predict-eval-b
272 rows (shard a), as predict-base-a; the adapter channel points at the experiment's adapter
200 rows (shard b); concatenate a then b as qwen3.5-4b-tuned predictions
scored locally: compare --matrix comparison-matrix.json (all three systems), then decision-report
